t509.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records al-Aswad ibn Yazīd ibn Qays al-Nakhaʿī, Abū ʿAmr or Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, as a mukhaḍram, trustworthy, prolific, and a jurist, of the second generation, and he died in 74 or 75 AH.
as: He was trustworthy and had sound hadiths.
al-ʿIjlī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
كوفي جاهلي ثقة، رجل صالح فقيه.
A trustworthy Kufan who lived in the pre-Islamic period, a righteous man and jurist.
الحكم بن عتيبة, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
He was among the jurists and leading figures of Kufa.
He was trustworthy and had sound hadiths.
أن الأسود كان يصوم في اليوم الشديد الحر حتى يسود لسانه من الحر
Ibrāhīm says he would fast on intensely hot days until his tongue darkened from the heat.
رياح النخعي, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
كان الأسود يصوم في السفر حتى يتغير لونه من العطش في اليوم الحار
Riyāḥ says al-Aswad fasted while traveling even on a hot day, until thirst affected his complexion.
حنش بن الحارث, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
رأيت الأسود قد ذهبت إحدى عينيه من الصوم.
Ḥanash says he saw that al-Aswad had lost the use of one eye from fasting.
ما بالعراق رجل أكرم علي من الأسود.
No man in Iraq is dearer to me than al-Aswad.
Shuʿbah calls this a mainstay of the people of Kufa.
